parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Nemalion, derived from Ancient Greek νῆμα (nêma).

parole.significato: any parrot of the Nestor taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Nestor.

parole.significato: any plant of the Neptunia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Neptunia.

parole.significato: black-crowned night heron (Nycticorax nycticorax)
parole.testo: From translingual Nycticorax, from Latin nycticorax, from Ancient Greek νυκτικόραξ (nuktikórax, literally “night crow”).

parole.significato: obelia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Obelia, derived from Ancient Greek ὀβελός (obelós, “spit, rod”).

parole.significato: toothed whale
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from translingual Odontoceti.

parole.significato: synonym of gambero di mare (“European lobster”)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Homarus.

parole.significato: any plant of the Oncoba taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Oncoba, of Arabic origin.

parole.significato: oxyuris
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Oxyuris. By surface analysis, ossi- + -uro.

parole.significato: pangasius
parole.testo: From translingual Pangasius.

parole.significato: any lichen of the taxonomic genus Parmelia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Parmelia, derived from Latin parma (“shield”).

parole.significato: paspalum (plant of the genus Paspalum)
parole.testo: From translingual Paspalum, from Hellenistic Ancient Greek πάσπαλος (páspalos, “type of millet”).

parole.significato: a plant in the genus Pedalium: Pedalium murex
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Pedalium, from Ancient Greek πηδάλιον (pēdálion).

parole.significato: any jellyfish of the Pelagia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Pelagia, derived from Ancient Greek πελάγιος (pelágios, “of the sea”), derived from πέλαγος (pélagos, “sea”).

parole.significato: any of voles of the subgenus Microtus (Pitymys)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Pitymys, derived from Ancient Greek πίτυς (pítus, “pine”) + μῦς (mûs, “mouse, rat”).

parole.significato: any of the taxonomic genus Plocamium of algae
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Plocamium, derived from Ancient Greek πλόκαμος (plókamos, “tress”).

parole.significato: poa
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Poa, from Ancient Greek πόα (póa, “fodder”).

parole.significato: any member of the Polistes taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Polistes, from Ancient Greek πολιστής (polistḗs, “city-founder”).

parole.significato: any member of the Pongo taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Pongo, from Kongo mpongi, mpungu.

parole.significato: purslane (any plant of the family Portulacaceae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Portulaca, from Latin portulāca. Doublet of porcacchia.

parole.significato: any plant of the Potamogeton taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Potamogeton, from Latin potamogēton, from Ancient Greek ποταμογείτων (potamogeítōn).

parole.significato: any rodent of the Proechimys taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Proechimys, derived from Latin prō- + Ancient Greek ἐχῖνος (ekhînos, “hedgehog”) + μῦς (mûs, “mouse, rat”).

parole.significato: protozoan
parole.testo: From translingual Protozoa.

parole.significato: prunasin
parole.testo: From translingual Prunus + -ina.

parole.significato: any member of the genus Psophus.
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Psophus.

parole.significato: puya
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Puya.

parole.significato: any insect in the Rosalia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Rosalia.

parole.significato: chamois
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Rupicapra.

parole.significato: any tunicate of the Sarpa taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Salpa.

parole.significato: a creeping zinnia, a plant in the genus Sanvitalia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Sanvitalia.

parole.significato: scolopacid (member of the Scolopacidae taxonomic family)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Scolopacidae, derived from the name of the genus Scolopax, from Ancient Greek σκολόπαξ (skolópax, “woodcock”).

parole.significato: a palm of the Serenoa taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Serenoa, named after botanist Sereno Watson (1826–1892).

parole.significato: any of the genus Serrasalmus of piranhas
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Serrasalmus, derived from Latin serra (“saw”) + salmō (“salmon”).

parole.significato: any member of the Sparidae taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Sparidae, derived from Latin sparus (“spear, javelin”).

parole.significato: synonym of idromante
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Spelerpes, from σπήλαιον (spḗlaion, “cave”) + ἕρπω (hérpō, “I crawl”).

parole.significato: spirochete
parole.testo: From translingual Spirochaeta.

parole.significato: spirogyra
parole.testo: From translingual Spirogyra.

parole.significato: any member of the Squalidae taxonomic family
parole.testo: From translingual Squalidae, from the name of the genus Squalus, from Latin squālus.

parole.significato: stapelia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Stapelia.

parole.significato: oilbird (Steatornis caripensis)
parole.testo: From translingual Steatornis.

parole.significato: any fungus of the genus Stereum
parole.testo: From translingual Stereum, from Ancient Greek στερεός (stereós, “firm, solid”).

parole.significato: sternbergia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Sternbergia.

parole.significato: stevia (plant of the genus Stevia)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Stevia, taxonomic genus named after 16ᵗʰ century Spanish botanist Pedro Jaime Esteve (latinized as Petrus Jacobus Stevus).

parole.significato: tamandua
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Tamandua, of Tupian origin.

parole.significato: common tansy (Tanacetum vulgare)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Tanacetum.

parole.significato: any nematode of the Thelazia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Thelazia, from Ancient Greek θηλάζω (thēlázō, “to suck”).

parole.significato: any plant in the Terminalia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Terminalia, from Late Latin terminālis.

parole.significato: hartwort
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Tordylium, from Ancient Greek τορδύλιον (tordúlion).

parole.significato: honey locust tree (Gleditsia triacanthos)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Gleditsia triacanthos.

parole.significato: tridacna (clam of the genus Tridacna)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Tridacna, from the neuter plural Latin tridacna, from Ancient Greek τρίδακνος (trídaknos), derived from τρι- (tri-, “three”) + δάκνω (dáknō, “to bite”).

parole.significato: thunbergia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Thunbergia.

parole.significato: synonym of renio
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Uralium.

parole.significato: stargazer (perciform fish in the family Uranoscopidae)
parole.testo: From translingual Uranoscopus, from Ancient Greek οὐρᾰνός (ourănós, “sky, heaven”) + σκοπός (skopós, “gazer”). By surface analysis, urano- + -scopo.

parole.significato: any member of the Urolophus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Urolophus.

parole.significato: a mite of species Varroa destructor
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Varroa, named after Roman polymath Mārcus Terentius Varrō.

parole.significato: veratrum, white hellebore (Veratrum album)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Veratrum, from Latin vērātrum (“hellebore”).

parole.significato: any plant of the Wahlenbergia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from translingual Wahlenbergia.

parole.significato: the Xerus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Xerus, from Ancient Greek ξηρός (xērós, “dry; lean”).

parole.significato: xiphosauran
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Xiphosura, from Ancient Greek ξῐ́φος (xĭ́phos) + οὐρά (ourá). By surface analysis, xifo- + -uro.

parole.significato: any beetle of the Zabrus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Zabrus, from Ancient Greek ζαβρός (zabrós, “voracious”).

parole.significato: any member of the Zalophus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Zalophus.

parole.significato: zamia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Zamia.

parole.significato: any plant of the Zantedeschia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Zantedeschia, from the name of Italian botanist Giovanni Zantedeschi.

parole.significato: a member of the Zea taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Zea, from Latin zēa (“spelt”), from Ancient Greek ζειά (zeiá).
